## Auckland Kitchen Pipe Repair Checklist

A non-emergency leaking kitchen pipe in a 2-bedroom Auckland apartment should be straightforward to quote and book within 3 days if you give plumbers the right details up front. Your budget of **NZD 250–450** is reasonable for a small repair, depending on access, parts, and after-hours timing.

## What to Ask Before You Book

- **Availability:** Can you attend within **3 days**?
- **Callout fee:** Is there a fixed inspection fee, and is it applied to the repair if you proceed?
- **Scope:** Does the quote cover **diagnosis, labour, parts, and tidy-up**?
- **Access:** Have you done apartment work before, including building access, parking, and body corporate rules?
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/c/c4/D%C3%BClmen%2C_Alte_Brennerei_L%C3%B6hning_--_2015_--_8609-13.jpg Alt=Access:** Have you done apartment work before, including building access, parking, and body corporate rules?, Request.
- **Leak details:** Do you need photos or a video before confirming the job?
- **Parts:** Will you supply the replacement pipe/fitting, and are parts included in the quote?
- **Price basis:** Is it a **fixed quote** or an **hourly rate**?
- **Timing:** What arrival window can you offer, and how long should the repair take?
- **Insurance:** Are you covered for public liability and accidental damage?
- **Guarantee:** What warranty applies to workmanship and replacement parts?

## Quote Comparison Checklist

| Checkpoint | What to confirm | Good sign | Watch out for |
|---|---|---|---|
| Availability | Can they fit you in within 3 days? | Clear booking window | Vague “soon” replies |
| Pricing | Fixed quote or hourly estimate | Itemised quote | Hidden callout or travel fees |
| Scope | Leak diagnosis + repair + cleanup | Clear inclusions | “Extra if needed” with no detail |
| Parts | Are fittings/materials included? | Parts listed separately or included | No mention of parts at all |
| Access | Apartment/building logistics | They ask for access info early | No experience with apartments |
| Warranty | Workmanship and parts cover | Written warranty period | No warranty stated |
| Receipt | GST invoice and job description | Full invoice issued | Cash-only, no paperwork |

## Best Way to Compare 3 Quotes

- Compare on **total landed cost**, not just the headline price.
- Prefer the plumber who gives a **written itemised quote** with:
  - callout or inspection fee
  - labour estimate
  - parts estimate
  - GST
  - timeframe
- If one quote is much lower, ask whether it excludes:
  - access fees
  - minor parts
  - follow-up visit
  - disposal/cleanup
- For your budget, a strong quote usually explains whether the job is:
  - a simple fitting replacement
  - a pipe section repair
  - a more involved leak trace and fix

## Warranty and Receipt Details to Request

- **Workmanship warranty:** Ask for at least a short written warranty on labour.
- **Parts warranty:** Confirm the manufacturer warranty on any replaced fittings.
- **Invoice/receipt should include:**
  - plumber’s business name and NZBN if available
  - date of service
  - address of the apartment
  - description of the leak repair
  - parts used
  - labour charged
  - GST amount
  - total paid
  - warranty terms or reference
- **Before paying:** Make sure the leak has been tested and the area left dry.
- **After the job:** Keep photos of the repaired area and the invoice in case the leak returns.

## Quick Booking Script

- “I have a non-urgent leaking kitchen pipe in a 2-bedroom Auckland apartment. I’d like it repaired within 3 days. Can you provide a written quote, confirm your callout fee, and tell me what warranty and invoice details you provide?”

## Sources

- Consumer NZ on hiring tradespeople: https://www.consumer.org.nz/articles/hiring-a-tradie
- Auckland Council building and plumbing guidance: https://www.aucklandcouncil.govt.nz/
- New Zealand Consumer Guarantees Act overview: https://www.consumerprotection.govt.nz/general-help/consumer-laws/consumer-guarantees-act/
